text.p: These are the leading stories in the Moroccan press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Opposition parties say they are ready to take over responsibilities of government.
- Finance Minister Kabbaj says Morocco will be back on international capital markets if it replaces costly short-term payment of debt by soft loans.
- Finance Minister Kabbaj will visit Spain on October 24 to discuss Moroccan debt, hoping for its conversion as was the case with France.
- State-owned airline Royal Air Maroc, instead of bidding for purchase of foreign company, should think of satisfying passengers on domestic flights who repeatedly complain of delays.
- President of Parliament Jalal Essaid, re-elected with narrow margin, unable to hold usual oral question session broadcast live after MPs fail to agree on representatives.
- Economic pickup following steady delivery of energy, hydrocarbons and electricity after five-month slump and application of penalty on tax evasion starting in July.
